G7900:
καταπολεμέω fut. ήσω
to war down, i. e. to exhaust by war, subdue completely, reduce, Lat. debellare, Thuc., Xen.: in pres. to attempt to subdue, Thuc.: —Pass., ἐλπίζοντες [τὴν πόλιν] καταπεπολεμῆσθαι id.
G7902:
καταπραύνω fut. υ^νῶ
to soften down, appease, Plat.
G7904:
καταπτήσσω fut. ‐πτήξω 3rd dual epic aor2 καταπτήτην poet. part. καταπτα^κών perf. κατέπτηχα epic part. καταπεπτηώς
1. to crouch down, to lie crouching or cowering, Hom., Hes.
2. c. acc. to cower beneath, Plut.
G7908:
καταργυρόω fut. ώσω
I. to cover with silver:—Pass., καταργυρωμένος (ionic for κατηργ‐) silvered, Hdt.
II. to buy or bribe with silver, κατηργυρωμένος Soph.
G7909:
καταρράκτης καταρ‐ράκτης, ου, [καταρρήγνυμι] [καταράσσω]
I. as adj. down-rushing, τὸν καταρράκτην ὀδόν (attic for οὐδόν) to the downward entrance [of Hades], Soph.
II. as Subst. broken water, a waterfall, Lat. cataracta, Strab.
2. a kind of portcullis, Plut.
3. a sea-bird, so called from rushing down upon its prey, a gull, Ar.
G7911:
καταρρέω fut. ‐ρεύσομαι fut. ‐ρυήσομαι perf. ‐ερρύηκα aor2 pass. ‐ερρύην
I. to flow down, Il., Hdt., attic
2. of men, to stream or rush down, Ar., Thuc.
3. of fruit, leaves, etc., to fall off, Xen.
4. to fall in ruins, Dem.
5. κ. εἴς τινα to come to, fall to the lot of, Theocr., Bion.
II. κ. φόνῳ to run down with blood, Eur.; so in Mid., Plut.
G7912:
καταρρήγνυμι and ‐ύω fut. ‐ρήξω
I. to break down, τὴν γέφυραν Hdt.; μέλαθρα Eur.
2. to tear in pieces, rend, Dem.:—Mid., κατερρήξαντο τοὺς κιθῶνας they rent their coats, Hdt.
3. in Soph. Ant. 675 τροπὰς καταρρήγνυσι [ἡ ἀναρχία] breaks up armies and turns them to flight.
II. Pass., aor2 κατερράγην [α^], with perf. act. κατέρρωγα: — to be broken down, to be thrown down and broken, Hdt.
2. to fall or rush down, to break or burst out, of storms, id.; of tears, Eur.:—metaph., ὁ πόλεμος κατερράγη Ar.
3. to be broken in pieces, Αἴγυπτος μελάγγαιός τε καὶ κατερρηγμένη with black and crumbling soil, Hdt.
B. καταράσσω
attic ‐ττω fut. ξω
I. to dash down, break in pieces, τοὺς λοιπούς κατήραξεν ἐς τὸν Κιθαιρῶνα drove them shattered to Cithaerae, Hdt.; τὸ στράτευμα κατηράχθη εἰς τὰ τειχίσματα Thuc.
II. intr. to fall down, fall headlong, Plut.
G7913:
καταρρίπτω fut. ψω
to throw down, overthrow, Aesch.
G7914:
κατάρχω fut. ξω
I. to make beginning of a thing, c. gen., Aesch.; ὁδοῦ κατάρχειν to lead the way, Soph.:— rarely c. acc. to begin a thing, Plat.:—c. part. to begin doing, Xen.
2. to honour, Eur.
II. Mid. to make a beginning, to begin, like Act., c. gen., id., Plat.; also c. acc., Eur.: absol., κατάρχεται μέλος is beginning, id.
2. in religious sense, to begin the sacrificial ceremonies, Νέστωρ χέρνιβά τ’ οὐλοχύτας τε κατήρχετο Nestor began [the sacrifice] with the washing of hands and sprinkling the barley on the victim's head, Od.; κατάρχομαι I begin the function, Eur.:—c. gen., κατάρχεσθαι τοῦ τράγου to make a beginning of the victim, i. e. consecrate him for sacrifice by cutting off the hair of his forehead, Ar.; πῶς δ’ αὖ κατάρξει θυμάτων; Eur.
b. to sacrifice, slay, id.:—Pass., σὸν κατῆρκται σῶμα hath been devoted, id.
c. simply, to strike, Plut.
G7916:
κατασιγάω fut. ήσομαι
to become silent, Plat.
G7917:
κατασιωπάω fut. ήσομαι
I. to be silent about a thing, Dem.
II. Causal, to make silent, silence, Xen.: Mid. to cause silence, id.
G7920:
κατασκευή κατα‐σκευή, ἡ,
I. preparation, ἐν κατασκευῇ τοῦ πολέμου in preparing for it, Thuc.; the equipment of ships, engines, etc., id.
II. any kind of furniture that is fixed, opp. to what is movable (παρασκευή), buildings, fixtures, id.; but also, like παρασκευή, any furniture, Hdt., Thuc.
III. the state, condition, constitution of a thing, Eur., Plat.
IV. a device, trick, Aeschin.
G7921:
κατάσκιος κατά‐σκιος, ον [σκιά]
I. shaded or covered with something, Hes., Hdt., Aesch.
II. trans. overshadowing, Aesch., Eur., Ar.
G7923:
κατασπαταλάω
to live wantonly, to wanton, Anth.
G7924:
κατασπάω fut. άσω
I. to draw or pull down, κ. τὰς νῆας to haul ships down to the sea, Hdt.; κ. σημεῖα to pull the flags down (in token of defeat), Thuc.; κ. τινὰ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἵππου Xen.
II. to quaff or swallow down, Lat. deglutire, Ar.
G7925:
κατασπείρω fut. ‐σπερῶ
I. to sow thickly: metaph., ἀνίας κ. to sow a crop of sorrows, Soph.
2. to beget, τέκνα Eur.
II. to scatter over, as in sowing, c. gen., Plut.
III. to besprinkle, Anth.
G7926:
κατασπεύδω fut. σω
to press, urge, or hasten on, Aeschin.
G7927:
κατασπουδάζομαι [with aor1 and perf. pass.]
Dep., to be very earnest or serious, Hdt.; οὐδαμῶς κατεσπουδασμένος ἀνήρ id.
G7928:
καταστασιάζω fut. άσω
I. to form a counter-party in the state, Plut.
II. Pass. to be factiously opposed or overpowered, Xen., Dem.
G7932:
καταστρατοπεδεύω fut. σω
I. to put into cantonments, encamp, Xen.: to station a fleet, id.
II. Mid. to take up quarters, encamp, id.
G7933:
κατατάσσω attic ‐ττω fut. ξω
I. to draw up in order, arrange, τὴν στρατιάν Xen.
2. to appoint, ἐπί τι to do a thing, Dem.
II. κατατάξασθαί τινι to make arrangements with one, id.
G7934:
κατατείνω fut. ‐τενῶ aor1 ‐έτεινα perf. ‐τέτα^κα
I. to stretch or draw tight, Il., Hdt.; κ. τὰ ὅπλα to draw the cables taut, Hdt.
2. to stretch so as to torture, Dem., etc.
3. to stretch or draw in a straight line, Hdt.
4. to hold tight down, Plut.
II. intr. to stretch oneself: hence,
1. to extend or run straight towards, Lat. tendere, Hdt., Xen.: absol. to extend, Hdt.
2. to strive against, strive earnestly, be vehement, Eur., Xen.: aor1 part., with all one's might, λέγω κατατείνας Plat.
G7935:
κατατέμνω fut. ‐τεμῶ aor2 κατέτα^μον
1. to cut in pieces, cut up, Hdt., Ar., etc.: so in Mid., Eur.:— Pass., τελαμῶσι κατατετμημένοις with regularly cut bandages, Hdt.; σπλάγχνα κατατετμημένα Ar.
2. κ. χώρην ἐς διώρυχας to cut it up into ditches or canals, Hdt.; κατετέτμηντο τάφροι ἐπὶ τὴν χώραν Xen.
3. c. dupl. acc. κ. τινὰ καττύματα to cut him into strips, Ar.:—Pass., κατατμηθείην λέπαδνα may I be cut up into straps, id.
4. κ. τὸν Πειραιᾶ to lay it out for building, Arist.:—Pass., ἡ πόλις κατατέτμηται τὰς ὁδοὺς ἰθείας has its streets cut straight, Hdt.
5. to cut into the ground, κατετέτμηντο τάφροι there were trenches cut, Xen.
G7937:
κατατήκω doric ‐τάκω fut. ‐τήξω
I. trans. to melt away, to make to fall away, Hdt.
II. Pass., with perf. act. κατατέτηκα, to melt or be melting away, Od., Hdt., attic
G7939:
κατατρίβω fut. ψω perf. ‐τέτρι^φα
to rub down or away; hence,
1. of clothes, to wear out, Theogn., Plat.
2. of persons, to wear out, exhaust, Thuc.: —Pass. to be quite worn out, Ar., Xen.
3. of Time, to wear it away, get rid of it, Lat. diem terere, Dem., Aeschin.: κ. τὸν βίον to employ it fully, Xen.; so in perf. pass. to pass one's whole time, κατατέτριμμαι στρατευόμενος id.
4. of property, to squander, id.
G7941:
κατατρώγω fut. ‐τρώξομαι aor2 κατ‐έτρα^γον
to gnaw in pieces, eat up, Ar.; c. gen., Plut.
G7942:
κατατυγχάνω fut. ‐τεύξομαι
to hit one's mark, to be successful, Dem.
G7943:
καταφαίνω fut. ‐φα^νω
I. to declare, make known, Pind.
II. Pass., fut. ‐φα^νήσομαι, aor2 κατ‐εφάνην [α^], to become visible, appear, Hhymn., Hdt.
2. to be quite clear or plain, Hdt., Plat.; κατεφάνη τῷ Δαρείῳ τεχνάζειν it was apparent to Darius that he was playing tricks, Hdt.
G7944:
καταφερής κατα‐φερής, ές [φέρομαι]
I. going down, εὖτε ἂν κ. γίνηται ὁ ἥλιος when the sun is near setting, Hdt.; of ground, sloping downwards, Lat. declivis, Xen.
II. inclined, Lat. proclivis, pronus, πρὸς οἶνον Plut.
G7946:
καταφθορά καταφθορά, ἡ, [καταφθείρω]
1. destruction, death, Eur.
2. metaph. confusion, φρενῶν Aesch.
G7947:
καταφλέγω fut. ξω
to burn down, burn up, consume, πυρί Il., Hes., etc.:—Pass. to be burnt down, Thuc.
G7950:
καταφυγή καταφυ^γή, ἡ,
I. a refuge, place of refuge, Hdt., Eur.: c. gen., κ. κακῶν refuge from evils, Eur., Thuc.
II. a way of escape, excuse, Dem.
G7952:
καταφυτεύω fut. σω
to plant, Plut., Luc.
G7953:
καταχαίρω
to exult over, c. dat., Hdt.; absol., καταχαίρων with malignant joy, id.
G7955:
καταχαλκόω fut. ώσω
to cover with brass, Hdt.
G7958:
καταχρυσόω fut. ώσω
I. to cover with gold-leaf, gild, Hdt.
II. to make golden (i. e. splendid), Plut.
G7960:
καταχώννυμι fut. ‐χώσω
to cover with a heap, ὁ νότος κατέχωσέ σφεας the South wind buried them in sand, Hdt.; κ. τινὰ λίθοις Ar.
G7961:
καταχωρίζω fut. attic ιῶ
to set in a place, place in position, Xen.:—Pass. to take up a position, id.
G7964:
κατεπείγω fut. ξω
I. to press down, depress, Il.
2. to press much, press hard, drive on, urge on, impel, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
II. intr. to hasten, make haste, Xen.
G7968:
κατευθύ
straight forward, Xen.
G7971:
κατοικοδομέω fut. ήσω
I. to build upon or in a place, Xen.
II. to build away, i. e. to squander in building, Plut.
G7972:
κάτοικος κάτ‐οικος,
a settler, Aesch.
G7974:
κατόπισθεν
I. behind, after, in the rear, Hom.; c. gen., Od.
II. of Time, hereafter, afterwards, henceforth, id.
G7975:
κάτοπτρον κάτ‐οπτρον, ου, τό, [ὄψομαι, fut. of ὁράω]
I. a mirror, Lat. speculum, Eur.
II. metaph. a mere reflexion (not a reality), Aesch.
G7976:
κατορθόω fut. ώσω
I. to set upright, erect, Eur.:—metaph. to keep straight, set right, Soph.
2. to accomplish successfully, bring to a successful issue, Plat., Dem.: —Pass. to succeed, prosper, Hdt., Eur.; δρᾶν κατώρθωσαι thou hast rightly purposed to do, Aesch.
II. intr. as in Pass. to go on prosperously, succeed, Thuc., Xen.; τὸ κατορθοῦν success, Dem.
G7977:
κατόρθωσις [from κατορθόω] κατόρθωσις, εως
a setting straight: successful accomplishment of a thing, success, Arist.
G7978:
κατορύσσω attic ‐ττω fut. ξω fut. pass. ‐ορυ^χήσομαι
to bury in the earth, Hdt.; ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν κατώρυξε buried head downwards, id.; ἐν τῇ κεφαλῇ Ar.
G7979:
κατορχέομαι fut. ήσομαι
Dep. to dance in triumph over, treat despitefully, Lat. insultare, Hdt.
G7982:
κάτοχος κάτοχος, ον [κατέχω]
I. holding down, holding fast, tenacious, Plut.
II. pass. kept down, held fast, overpowered, overcome, Aesch., Soph.; κάτοχος subject to him, Eur.
G7985:
κάτωθεν [κάτω]
I. from below, up from below, Aesch., Plat.:—also, from the low country, from the coast, Hdt.
II. below, beneath, where κάτω would be required by our idiom, Soph., Plat., etc.
G7986:
καυλός καυλός, οῦ,
I. the shaft of a spear, Il.: the hilt of a sword, id.
II. the stalk of a plat, Ar., etc.
G7988:
κέγχρος κέγχρος, ὁ,
I. millet, Hes., Hdt., etc.; of a single grain, Hdt.
II. anything in small grains, as the spawn of fish, id.
G7989:
κέδρινος κέδρι^νος, η, ον
of cedar, Il., Eur.
[from κέδρος]
G7991:
κενολογέω κενολογέω, φυτ. ‐ήσω
to talk emptily, Arist.
[from κενολόγος]
G7992:
κενοτάφιον κενο‐τάφιον, ου, τό, [τάφος]
an empty tomb, cenotaph, Xen.
G7993:
κεντέω [epic inf. κένσαι as if from κέντω]
1. to prick, goad, spur on, Il., Ar.
2. of bees and wasps, to sting, Ar., Theocr.
3. generally, to prick, stab, Pind., Soph., etc.: to torture, Xen.: metaph., σὺν δόλωι κ. to stab in the dark, Soph.
G7996:
κεράστης κεράστης, ου,
horned, ἔλαφος Soph., Eur.:—fem. κεραστίς, ίδος, of Io, Aesch.
